history.notes: Declares `<serialsettings>2400 8 none 1 none 232</serialsettings>`, so the controller sets the bound RS-232 port to 2400 8N1, the PRT3's factory default (section [016] options [2] and [3] OFF, per Paradox's APR3-PRT3 ASCII Protocol Programming Instructions), instead of leaving it at whatever it was last set to. The guide now requires 2400 instead of letting the dealer pick a baud: a PRT3 programmed to 9600, 19200 or 57600 must be set back to 2400.

Fix: Composer's System Design tree could show this driver as a blank row with no name. Composer draws the device tiles at 16 and 32 px and this build shipped 32 and 300 px ones, so the row rendered as an oversized blank smear. The tiles are re-cut at 16/32 px from the same art. No control changes.

Certification pass: the packaged Version history now renders its formatting instead of shipping raw markdown, plus documentation corrections verified line by line against the driver's own manifest and code.
Documentation rebuilt to the IntegrateIT commissioning-guide standard: uniform sections, honest contracts, verified claim-by-claim against the code.

Pre-ship adversarial review hardening (state fidelity + the never-suppress-an-alarm contract), no protocol changes: · Special disarm events (system-event group G022 - WinLoad disarm, one-touch stay/instant disarm, voice-module disarm, auto-arm cancelled) now report the area as Disarmed and fire `Area Disarmed`. These paths emit no G013-018 disarm event, so G022 is their only signal; previously the area read a stale `Armed` until the next status poll. The G022 cancel-alarm sub-event (N004) still only clears the alarm and never fabricates a disarm. · A zone/fire/panic alarm whose area field is 000 (all-areas / global) is no longer silently dropped: it still fires `Area In Alarm` and surfaces status, upholding the driver's standing contract that an alarm is never suppressed even when it has no single area to pin it to. · Added regression tests: G022 special disarm (and the N004 non-disarm guard), global-area alarm never suppressed, an RA reply reassembled from byte-at-a-time serial chunks, and a NACKed (&fail) arm that must never fabricate an armed state.
